stops.note: 'the whole', from universus; in Roman law any corporation or guild
a guild of students or masters; Bologna's university traditionally dates to 1088, and Emperor Frederick Barbarossa's Authentica Habita of the 1150s protected travelling scholars
Paris's masters won a royal charter from Philip II in 1200 and papal statutes in 1215
teaching at Oxford is recorded from 1096, and Cambridge was founded by scholars who left Oxford in 1209

current_meaning: an institution of higher education and research that awards degrees
